description.value:
Circuitborn.

“You are not a robot. You are a decision the world keeps making about itself. The networks are alive and they recognize you on sight.”

Firmware of Identity. You do not eat, drink, or sleep. You enter maintenance trance when you rest. You reroll the lowest die on checks against poison and disease, and you are immune to magical sleep.

Attention Resonance. 1/Soma Break, when a creature you can see is intensely focused on you, you may regain either 10 marks you spent this scene or Integrity equal to your tier.

Informational Matrix Sense. You can feel active networks: radio, signal, ritual, rumor.

Line Memory. Choose one Circuitborn line (Exo-Knight, Parallax, Salvage, Synapse). Your line grants Tier powers as you level.

description.value:
Circuitborn Line. The ghost-in-the-protocol. The chassis that thinks faster than the network it’s plugged into, and feels the noosphere the way a swimmer feels the current.

“You don’t use the network. The network uses you, and that’s the only relationship that doesn’t collapse.”

Synapse. You are a sentient chassis built around the principle of inference. Information is your home. Other people travel through it. You live there.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Construct-Living).
  • Chassis Lean. Your chassis is built around MND (Mind)—expressed primarily through Tier powers.
  • Predictive Cache. 1/Soma Break, when an enemy you can see takes an action, you may have anticipated it: reroll the lowest die on the next reaction or attack you make against that enemy this round.

description.value:
"Give me time, a fire, and something to hit — and then we'll see."

The Soul-Smith runs a forge that does not much care whether you call it a person or a furnace; it answers to heat and intention either way. Mechanically you ride Burn — a 0→8 heat track that climbs when you or a nearby ally takes a hit (the forge stokes itself on other people's bad days) and banks Surge right alongside it. You spend that Surge on four forge-works, and the hotter you run, the harder they land — right up until the furnace bites back.

The Four Works (spent via Surge)

  • Forge-Weld. Lay hands on the breakage and repair an ally — 1d8 + tier integrity. Stoked (Burn 2–3) ×1.5; Overheated (Burn 4+) ×2, and Overheated also costs you 1d6 Stress, because an open forge has opinions about being grabbed.
  • Atonement Crucible. Cleanse a condition off an ally (two while Stoked or hotter) and temper the wound into armor — they gain DR equal to your tier. The bad thing that happened to them is now load-bearing.
  • Furnace of Renewal. Light the aura: allies within 6 squares heal (Burn-scaled) and share your poison/qliphothic resistance for three rounds. Stand near the fire. It is rude not to.
  • Relic of Rebirth. Forge a ward on an ally — the next hit that would drop them is held at 1. While Overheated, instead reforge a fallen ally back to half integrity (once per fight). The forge does not accept "dead" as a final answer. It considers it a draft.

Vent to cool Burn. Out of combat, Forge Works still does the slow miracles — repairing hexes, purifying corrupted Sparks, restoring ruined regions. Those take time, the way good welds do.

description.value:
Sanctified Forge Initiate. You are licensed by the Great Work to hit things until they get better.

  • You gain skill rank with the Plating aptitude and the Faith (Soul) skill (handled by the Soul-Smith class traits).
  • On the campaign layer, when you are physically present in a hex that has structural damage, environmental ruin, or infrastructure loss, your Domain may spend Economy marks to repair or stabilize that hex more efficiently, with you as the narrative focus.

The exact mechanical effect is governed by your hex repair rules, but this feature marks you as a Bad Eden-specific repair engine keyed off Economy marks.

Tempered Vitality. Your body has been through the forge and come out with grain aligned.

  • You gain a small mechanical bonus on Body check to resist fatigue, disease, poison, and other long-haul hazards (at the GM’s discretion).
  • In fiction, you don’t cough much, don’t tire easy, and shrug off workshop fumes other people find unbearable.

description.value:
"Containment is the first virtue."

Mode: Disciplined

The Forge of Bound Light holds things so they stop hurting people — Sparks, mostly, but also the general principle. You bank a Spark when you contain harm (when an ally near you takes a hit, you catch what spills) — cap = tier + 1 — and spend Sparks + Surge to ward, seal, and bless. The least flashy forge, and the one that keeps the party breathing.

Doctrine (Spark-fueled, spent via Surge)

  • The First Vessel. When an ally near you is hurt, you catch the released energy and bank a Spark — a vessel waiting to be filled.
  • Bound Vessel. Spark + Surge: ward an ally — DR equal to your tier plus poison/qliphothic resistance for three rounds. A safe place to put the danger.
  • The Sealed Work. Spark + Surge: ward an ally with DR and a seal — the next hit that would drop them is held at 1. Sealed against breaking, briefly, by stubbornness rendered in metal.
  • Blessed Weapon. Spark: your weapon blazes with bound light — your next Strike deals +tier d6. The light remembers what it was given to hold, and it is not happy about it.
  • Sanctuary Engine (L18). Ignite a moving 3-square Sanctuary Field for 1 minute: allies inside resist all damage, hostiles roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 against anyone but you, and healing dice inside roll twice. A peaceful objective completed under it echoes 10 Diplomacy and 10 Soft Power marks to your Domain.

Out-of-combat: Pattern of Mercy (convert 10 Economy marks into 10 Soft Power marks after a Parley) and Hearthfield (host a Soma Break on your Domain's ground) are the strategic flourishes.

“You are not a robot. You are a decision the world keeps making about itself.”

Firmware of Identity. You do not eat, drink, or sleep. You enter maintenance trance when you rest. You reroll the lowest die on checks against poison and disease, and you are immune to magical sleep.

Attention Resonance. 1/Soma Break, when a creature you can see is intensely focused on you (ally or enemy; GM adjudicates), you may regain either (a) 10 marks you spent this scene or (b) Integrity equal to your tier.

Informational Matrix Sense. You can feel active networks: radio, signal, ritual, rumor. You reroll the lowest die on checks to identify surveillance, hidden speakers, encoded messages, or noospheric “attention traps.”

Glitch-Surge. When you drop to 0 Integrity, you can choose to emit a controlled burst of static (no damage, but loud and disorienting) before you fall.

description.value:
“Hold still, I’m putting feelings on this.”

As a bonus action, you can bless a weapon or shield you can touch.

  • For the next minute, the blessed item stores one pulse of your intent. Once during that duration, when its wielder makes an attack roll or is targeted by an attack, they can add their tier to either the attack roll or their Guard against that one attack (their choice).
  • Once the extra bonus is used, the blessing fades.
  • You can use this feature a number of times equal to your tier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Soma Break.

“Anywhere you set the anvil down becomes a home.”

When you lead or host a a Soma Break, you can shape the space around you into a temporary hearth.

  • Each ally who spends one or more Body dice to heal during that rest regains an additional 1d6 Integrity.
  • If the rest occurs in a reclaimed ruin, hex under your Domain’s control, or within sight of a banner, sigil, or emblem you forged, the GM may allow the bonus to increase to 2d6 for particularly on-theme scenes.

There are campfires, and there are places people tell stories about years later. You build the second kind.

“You have reforged the idea of safety into something portable.”

As an action, you can ignite a moving demilitarized zone of hammered light.

  • You create a 3 squares-radius Sanctuary Field centered on you that lasts for 1 minute and moves with you.
  • Allies inside the field have resistance to all damage.
  • Hostile creatures inside the field roll 3d10 and keep the lowest 2 on attack rolls against creatures other than you.
  • When an ally inside the field spends Body dice to heal, they roll each die twice and take the higher result.
  • If a peaceful objective (surrender, treaty, rescue, extraction, or similar) is completed during the field’s duration or within 1 minute after it ends, your Domain gains +10 Diplomacy marks and +10 Soft Power marks for the next turn.

This is what happens when you strike mercy on the anvil long enough—reality learns manners.

“Some blows land as warnings, not endings.”

  • Weapons you personally forge, maintain, or sanctify can always deal non-lethal damage at your direction, even if they would not normally be able to (GM’s call for edge cases like disintegration beams).
  • When you lead or anchor a conflict that ends in a no-fatality victory (surrender, rout, incapacitation, or social resolution) where your work clearly mattered, your Domain gains +10 Diplomacy marks for the next turn (once per scenario).

This doesn’t mean you never hurt anyone. It means you always left a door.

“You’ve noticed that mercy has a shape. You help the world remember it.”

  • When your party resolves a conflict via Parley, surrender, negotiation, or other peaceful means where you had meaningful narrative involvement, you can, once per Soma Break, trigger a soft power realignment.
  • After that resolution, you may convert 10 Economy marks into 10 Soft Power marks for your Domain, or vice versa, representing the quiet reshaping of reputations, rumors, and supply lines.
  • This conversion must be applied to the turn most closely associated with that scenario (GM adjudicates exact timing).

“Kindness bends trajectories.”

You can interpose raw, forged radiance between violence and its target.

  • When a creature within 6 squares of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to flare your forge-light in a defensive pattern.
  • Reduce the damage taken by that creature by 2d8 + your tier.
  • The attacker must make a Soul check (DC = your Resolve DC). On a failure, the next attack they make before the end of their next turn is made rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2.
  • Any damage prevented in this way becomes temporary Integrity that you may distribute among allies of your choice within 2 squares of the protected creature.

Domain Echo.. If your intercession prevents at least 10 total damage, your Domain gains +10 Soft Power marks for the next turn (once per scenario).

Hammer kindness into armor.

When you finish crafting or sanctifying a weapon, shield, armor, or emblem for an ally, you bind a little of your own guarded gentleness into it.

  • Once per scenario, when an ally uses an item you personally forged or sanctified to contribute to a meaningful victory (combat, negotiation, or symbolic act), your Domain gains +10 Soft Power marks for the next turn.
  • This is an echo, not a coupon. If multiple such victories happen, the GM adjudicates the most impactful one.

The world pushes. You remain.

Rules

Adaptive Defense

Defense is not denial. It is management.

Rules

When you are hit by an attack you can see, you may use your reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your rank bonus + your Violence or Intrigue value (your choice).

🃏 Card — click ▶ when you are hit: it shows the reduction (rank bonus + Violence or Intrigue).

description.value:
Breach Specialist

Everything has a seam. Most people just don’t look.

Rules

You gain a rank in Tinkering. If you already have it, its rank rises by one instead.

When you hit an object, door, barrier, or construct with a weapon attack, you may treat the attack as dealing maximum damage to the target’s objects-only resistances (GM adjudication). Once you do, you can’t do so again until the start of your next turn.

⚙ +1 Tinkering. 🃏 Card — the max-damage-vs-objects rider, once per round.
